findings.evidence: review-protocol.md says to pass --model only when the configuration names no model or a different one. The skills still say to always forward it: .agent-sync/skills/spec-implement/SKILL.md:32,33,61,509,513, spec-feature/SKILL.md:31,32,924, spec-ship/SKILL.md:22,23,314, spec-specify/SKILL.md:37,38, and system/anti-drift-block.md:170. This is harmless at runtime: bind_review_model appends the same --model= flag when the model comes from the configuration, so the goal hash is identical. But the instructions disagree. The implementer marked this as a follow-up on purpose.
findings.correction: In a follow-up, change the skill and anti-drift wording to 'add --model=<actual-model> unless review_model in .specs/semantic/config.yaml names it', matching review-protocol.md.

findings.evidence: prepare_feature_review now applies review_budget, which adds the 200000 upper bound to every review entry point, not only goal, progression and delivery. A probe of `livespec validate <feature> --prepare-review spec --review-max-chars 250000` now exits 1 with 'BLOCKED: review_max_chars_out_of_bounds'; before this change it was accepted. refresh_goal of a saved goal whose flags carry --review-max-chars above 200000 now raises GoalRecompileError. The typer options in validator/cli.py:414 and validator/pipeline.py:373,437 still declare only min=1000. The bounds are also duplicated with validator/execution_mapping.py:43 (ge=1000, le=200000). The spec Edge Case says 'explicit or configured', so this matches the spec, but nothing tests it on those surfaces.
findings.correction: Optionally add max=200000 to the --review-max-chars typer options so users get a consistent usage error. Share one constant with execution_mapping.py when its size debt allows. Add a line to the changelog noting that budgets above 200000 are now refused on review prepare/ingest as well.

findings.evidence: A config.yaml whose top level is valid YAML but not a mapping (for example '- a') makes load_semantic_config return defaults silently (validator/semantic/config.py:73), so it does not stop with review_config_invalid. Probe: `delivery lane --model reviewer/v1 --json` exits 0 with a full lane and spec_review_not_current. Without --model the command fails closed with review_model_required. The spec lists only invalid YAML, non-UTF-8 bytes and an unreadable path, so this does not violate the spec.
findings.correction: Optionally treat a non-mapping top level as review_config_invalid in resolve_review_identity, or name it explicitly in the Edge Case.

findings.evidence: A review_model that is present but is not a string (for example `review_model: 7`) is treated as absent, so the first named review_reviewers entry becomes the reviewer silently. The Edge Case only describes the fallback when review_model is absent. This fails closed against receipts made by another model, but it can bind a goal to a reviewer the user did not mean.
findings.correction: Optionally refuse a non-string or placeholder review_model with review_config_invalid instead of falling back to the reviewer list.

findings.evidence: The text says '`livespec delivery lane|review` exit 2' when no model resolves. `livespec delivery review record` never resolves an identity: it does not take --model and cannot fail with review_model_required. Only `review prepare` and `review verify` can (the spec Edge Case states this correctly). README.md says the same thing more broadly: '`livespec delivery` take the reviewer model'.

ReviewIdentity.source is computed but no caller reads it, and an explicit placeholder --model ('default', 'unknown', blank) is refused even when the configuration names a model (tested in test_only_a_named_model_resolves). The second behavior matches the old goal render and the Edge Case. It is a deliberate choice that the User Flow diagram ('--model given? Yes -> use it') does not show.
findings.correction: None required. Optionally show the placeholder refusal in the User Flow.

findings.evidence: The tests cover AC-001 and SC-001 for goal render (spec-plan with and without --model), progression (CLI and API), delivery lane (configuration only, explicit model, required, budget), review verify, revision open, the implement-goal internal lane, unreadable configuration with --model on lane, goal render and progression, placeholders and stripping, review_reviewers fallback, non-ASCII budget flag, and short budget errors. Not covered: revision close, review prepare without --model with configuration only, and the pipeline next/update progression path. Reading the code, these use the same resolve_review_identity path.
findings.correction: Optional: add one case for `delivery revision close` and one for `delivery review prepare` with configuration only.
